transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because people keep acting like I’m making something out of nothing, but I’m not. It’s about my father’s death. I’ve been looking at the hospital records and some donation emails, and everyone says they all line up, but when I compare the timestamps and the missing attachments, and then certain people in the community suddenly avoid my questions… it’s obvious to me someone is hiding what really happened.

And I know that sounds like a lot, but I work with systems, I notice patterns. Like even at my job, small mismatches usually mean something got changed or someone doesn’t want you to see the full trail. So I guess I’m here because no one will take that seriously.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

I mean… no, not like a voice talking to me in an empty room, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes I’ll hear people talking in the hallway at work and I’ll wonder if it’s about me, but that’s different, that’s just—well, in offices people act like everything’s normal and then messages disappear or suddenly nobody remembers a conversation. So… I don’t think I’m hearing voices, no.
Since your father died, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day, nearly every day. I mean, I’ve been upset, obviously, and frustrated because when you’re trying to get straight answers and people keep acting like the paperwork is clean when it isn’t, it wears on you. 

But “depressed” is kind of a specific word, right? Like I still get up, I go to work, I deal with systems issues all day—actually there was this server migration last week that was a complete mess because nobody documented the dependencies—sorry. I guess what I’m saying is, I’ve been bothered and angry and preoccupied, but I’m not sure I’d describe it the way you asked.
If someone showed you clear proof that your father’s death was handled properly, would you believe it?

If it was actually clear proof, I mean… I’d look at it. I’m not unreasonable. But people keep saying “clear” when what they mean is the hospital records and those donation emails line up if you don’t look too closely.

When I compare the timestamps, and there are missing attachments, and then certain people in the community suddenly don’t want to answer basic questions—sorry, it reminds me of work, where someone says a log is clean but the audit trail has these little gaps—anyway, to me that doesn’t feel handled properly. It feels like someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.

So I guess… I’d believe real proof. But I haven’t seen that.
Before your father died, did you often feel that other people were hiding things from you or trying to harm you?

Before? Not really, no. I mean, I’ve always been the kind of person who notices when details don’t line up—at work that’s basically my job, you know, finding the missing piece in a system—but this particular thing, the feeling that people were keeping things from me, that really started after my father died.

It’s been… about nine months now, I guess. Since I started going through his records and old messages and trying to make sense of what happened. That’s when it started feeling like there were things being hidden.
Do you believe for certain that someone hid the truth about your father’s death?

Yeah… I do. I mean, people keep telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all match up, like that should just settle it, but when I actually compare the timestamps and see missing attachments, and then certain people in the community suddenly dodge simple questions—it’s hard not to see it.

It’s like at work when a system report says everything completed successfully, but the logs have gaps. You don’t just ignore that. So yes, to me it’s obvious someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.
Aside from your father’s death, do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or deceive you in other parts of your life?

Other parts of my life? Not really in the same way. I mean, at work people can be evasive sometimes—IT departments are like that, everyone says “it’s in the ticket” when it clearly isn’t—but I don’t think that’s the same thing.

What I keep coming back to is my father’s death. Everyone keeps saying the hospital records and the donation emails line up, but when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then certain community members avoid my questions… that’s the part that’s obvious to me. Someone is hiding what really happened there. Not, like, the whole world is after me. It’s that situation.
Has this belief about your father’s death caused serious problems in your daily functioning?

I mean… serious problems? I wouldn’t say serious in the sense that I can’t function. I still go to work, I handle my projects, I pay my bills, keep my normal routine. I’m not, you know, falling apart day to day.

It’s more that things get tense when I bring up my questions about my father’s records. With family, or some people in the community, they get uncomfortable or shut it down, and then suddenly I’m the difficult one. Which is frustrating, because in my job if something doesn’t add up, you’re supposed to ask questions. But outside of that, I’m still doing what I need to do.
Do you feel responsible for your father’s death?

Responsible? I don’t… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I keep thinking there were things I should’ve asked sooner, or looked at more closely, you know? Like when you miss a warning sign in a system and later everyone says it was “within normal parameters,” but you remember something felt off.

But responsible for his death… I don’t know. That’s a heavier word. I mostly feel like there are unanswered parts, and people want me to stop looking at them. I’m not saying I caused anything. It’s more like—I wish I’d known what to question earlier.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things? I don’t think so. I mean, not like… if you mean seeing a person in the room who isn’t there, no.

Sometimes I notice details other people miss, especially in documents or timestamps, but that’s not “seeing things,” that’s just paying attention. My coworkers joke that I can spot a misconfigured field from across the room, which—well, that’s because I’ve spent years staring at dashboards. But actual things other people couldn’t see? No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Did this belief that someone hid the truth about your father’s death come on suddenly?

Not suddenly, exactly. It’s been… maybe about nine months now. It started after my father died, when I was going through his records and old messages and trying to organize everything.

At first it was just practical stuff, like sorting files, passwords, paperwork—honestly, I had a whole spreadsheet because that’s just how I deal with things—but then certain things didn’t line up, and I kept coming back to them. So no, it wasn’t like I woke up one morning with this thought out of nowhere. It built up during that period after he died.
Do you still find yourself yearning intensely for your father or feeling preoccupied with missing him every day?

I mean… I miss him, sure. He was my dad. But “yearning intensely every day” sounds a little dramatic to me, or maybe I’m not understanding the phrasing.

Some days I think about him because something reminds me—like I’ll see some old technical manual or hear a phrase he used to say, and then my mind goes sideways into, you know, how people keep records, how families keep different versions of the same story. My uncle still has boxes of stuff in his garage, completely unorganized, which drives me crazy because if you don’t label things then later everyone acts like the missing pieces were never there.

But missing him every single day in that way… I don’t know. I wouldn’t put it like that. It’s more complicated than just missing him.
Since this started, have there been times when your thoughts were racing so fast that you could hardly keep up with them?

Racing? I’m not sure I’d call it that. I do think through things a lot, especially when there are inconsistencies, but that’s sort of how my job trained me to be—like if a system throws one weird error, you don’t just ignore it, you check the logs, the timestamps, the dependencies.

But thoughts going so fast I couldn’t keep up with them… no, I don’t think I’ve noticed that. It’s more like I get stuck on a thread and keep following it, not like everything is speeding past me.
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts have been hard to follow or seemed jumbled?

I don’t think so. Not in those words, anyway.

Sometimes people say I “over-explain” things, especially at work, because I’ll start with the main point and then realize there are three pieces of context they need or they’ll misunderstand it. Like with my dad’s records, if you don’t explain the sequence, people jump to the wrong conclusion. But hard to follow or jumbled… I haven’t really been told that.

I mean, my sister has said, “Can you just get to the point?” but that’s different, right? That’s more impatience than me not making sense.
Since this began, have there been stretches when you felt down or hopeless nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I don’t know if I’d say hopeless nearly every day for two weeks. I’ve had bad stretches, sure, but “nearly every day” and “at least two weeks” feels like you’re asking me to put a calendar grid over it, and I haven’t really tracked it like that.

Sometimes I get low, especially when things feel… unresolved, I guess. But then work picks up, or I get distracted fixing something, and it’s not the same all day. So I’m not sure. I wouldn’t confidently say yes to that.
Have you had any other beliefs that people were hiding things from you, apart from what happened with your father’s death?

Not really apart from that. I mean, it all kind of connects back to my dad.

It’s not like I walk around thinking everyone is hiding things from me in general. But with the hospital records and those donation emails, people keep saying, “It lines up, it’s all there,” and when I compare the timestamps and the missing attachments and then certain people in the community suddenly don’t answer direct questions… I don’t know how else to read that.

Sorry, I know I’m going off a bit. It’s just, if you’ve ever worked with logs, you know when something doesn’t match, you don’t just accept someone saying, “No, it’s fine.” To me it’s obvious someone is hiding what really happened around his death.

target_item.reason: The question is asking about depressive symptoms (feeling down or hopeless nearly every day for at least two weeks), which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d say hopeless nearly every day for two weeks. I’ve had bad stretches, sure, but “nearly every day” and “at least two weeks” feels like you’re asking me to put a calendar grid over it, and I haven’t really tracked it like that.

Sometimes I get low, especially when things feel… unresolved, I guess. But then work picks up, or I get distracted fixing something, and it’s not the same all day. So I’m not sure. I wouldn’t confidently say yes to that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed false belief extends beyond the bereavement context, which would favor a primary psychotic disorder over grief-related or depressive conditions.
doctor.question: Have you had any other beliefs that people were hiding things from you, apart from what happened with your father’s death?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and donation emails all line up, but when I compare the timestamps, missing attachments, and the way certain community members avoid my questions, it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the presence and scope of fixed suspicious beliefs that people are hiding things, which directly relates to delusions.

patient.answer:
Not really apart from that. I mean, it all kind of connects back to my dad.

It’s not like I walk around thinking everyone is hiding things from me in general. But with the hospital records and those donation emails, people keep saying, “It lines up, it’s all there,” and when I compare the timestamps and the missing attachments and then certain people in the community suddenly don’t answer direct questions… I don’t know how else to read that.

Sorry, I know I’m going off a bit. It’s just, if you’ve ever worked with logs, you know when something doesn’t match, you don’t just accept someone saying, “No, it’s fine.” To me it’s obvious someone is hiding what really happened around his death.

inference.note: Persistent, non-bizarre persecutory belief focused on a single theme for ~9 months, with preserved functioning and no hallucinations, formal thought disorder, mania, or clear major depressive episode. This narrows away F43.21 and F32.3.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a fixed, circumscribed persecutory belief that someone concealed the truth about the father's death, present for about nine months, developing gradually after the death. The belief is held with conviction despite others disagreeing, but there are no hallucinations, no broader bizarre delusional system, no clear thought disorganization, no manic syndrome, and no sustained major depressive episode. Functioning is largely preserved aside from interpersonal tension around the belief. This is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder.
